author: Matthew Baughman
title: SAC recommends the city of Eau Claire to hold a moratorium on data centers - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Baughman ,
8 hours ago
EAU CLAIRE — Members of the city of Eau Claire’s Sustainability Advisory Commission (SAC) on Wednesday discussed what policy they should consider when it comes to data center development.
SAC Chair Lily Strehlow said, “We as a committee began discussing data centers and learning about them together back in February. We did that because we knew in general there were a lot of environmental sustainability concerns with data centers, and we wanted to understand those so that we could work with the city to address those concerns. So since February, we’ve been learning and now we are moving towards making these recommendations.”
Part of the meeting centered around recommending the City Council pass a one-year moratorium, which would prevent data center development for a year as the city looks at its zoning code.
“Right now, the zoning code definition for a data center is really vague and captures potentially erroneous server rooms,” Strehlow said. “That needs some work so that we can be really specific in addressing the size of such a development.”
Currently, Eau Claire’s zoning code defines a data center as “A facility housing a large group of networked servers and associated equipment used by organizations for the remote storage, processing or distribution of large amounts of data.”
During the discussion, a member of the commission referenced past presentations focusing on data centers. While there is certainly an economic opportunity regarding their development, they said it was also key they minimize and manage any environmental risk.
A big consideration as well is that whether or not a data center is best for communities in the Chippewa Valley depends on the data center design and what the water and air resources are.
City Council member Andrew Werthmann, who serves as the council representative on the committee, said both residents who are opposed to and those open to potential development indicate an interest in more transparency.
A moratorium recommendation by the SAC was passed Wednesday, but Strehlow said it will be up to City Council in a future legislative session to take any official action.
City Council will also have an opportunity to extend the moratorium past one year if they wish to continue conversations.
If it were to move forward, she said the SAC will focus on what they want those environmental recommendations to be.
“We may be able to be specific or we may be able to make general recommendations that things like water be addressed,” she said. “We need to work through that as a committee so we can make the best recommendations that we can.”
This discussion and recommendation comes amid conversations regarding AI data center development in the Chippewa Valley. Most notably, a project in Menomonie faced community opposition and led to the city taking action to put the project on pause.
Other communities have also moved to this action, with Dane County signing an 18-month moratorium pausing zoning permits for “hyperscale” data center projects earlier in June.
Strehlow said being proactive about regulating data centers is the goal, as the moratorium is intended to give the city time to develop standards.
“We have a section in our zoning code that allows for supplemental standards for developments like data centers, and it even specifies data centers, but it’s missing those supplemental standards right now,” she said.
“We’ve had many public commenters last month, this month, and likely in future months. The public really cares about this topic, and throughout Wisconsin we’ve seen communities really caught off guard by these proposals. We want to make sure that we can have a really robust conversation that engages everyone to the best of our ability as a committee.”
